content.intro: This lesson covers integrating other protocols and frameworks within advanced fastapi features and extensibility. Use the supplied syllabus topics as the coverage checklist, then connect them to the worked example and the verification task.
content.why_it_matters: You will use integrating other protocols and frameworks to build APIs whose contracts and behavior are understandable to both clients and maintainers. The practical aim is a small, well-defined behavior with explicit assumptions, a predictable result and a testable edge case.

content_blocks.title: Core idea
content_blocks.text: Integrating Other Protocols and Frameworks matters because it is part of advanced fastapi features and extensibility. In practice, focus on a small, well-defined behavior with explicit assumptions, a predictable result and a testable edge case. A framework feature only helps when its assumptions match the application; keep input validation, business policy and side effects distinguishable.

items.title: Choosing REST, WebSockets, or another communication pattern
items.text: For choosing rest, websockets, or another communication pattern, identify which operation waits on I/O, which resources remain open, and what happens on timeout or disconnect. Async syntax does not make CPU-bound work faster or durable background jobs reliable by itself.

content_blocks.title: Worked example: Integrating Other Protocols and Frameworks
content_blocks.code:
from fastapi import FastAPI
from fastapi.middleware.cors import CORSMiddleware

app = FastAPI()
app.add_middleware(
    CORSMiddleware,
    allow_origins=["http://localhost:5173"],
    allow_credentials=True,
    allow_methods=["GET", "POST"],
    allow_headers=["Authorization", "Content-Type"],
)
content_blocks.expected_output: Browser requests from the listed development origin can pass the configured CORS policy for the allowed methods/headers.
content_blocks.run_instructions: Replace localhost with explicit trusted production origins; do not combine credentials with wildcard origins.
content_blocks.reset_steps: For read-only examples, no reset is needed. For any example that writes state, use a disposable local database/test fixture; record the starting state and clean up only lab data. Never use production credentials or real personal data.

Security examples are sketches, not complete production authentication or authorization systems.

hints: Start with “Starlette capabilities used by FastAPI” and state the required inputs, output and assumptions.

expected_output: A reviewable example or design note for Integrating Other Protocols and Frameworks, covering the PDF subtopics, expected behavior and at least one verification check.

common_mistakes.problem: Copying a code fragment without checking its assumptions.
common_mistakes.why: Installed versions, imported types, application structure and external services affect behavior.
common_mistakes.fix: State assumptions; check the versioned official docs; run a minimal local test and add one failure case.

common_mistakes.problem: Treating one happy-path response as proof of correctness.
common_mistakes.why: Invalid input, permissions, concurrency, timeouts and cleanup are not exercised by a single request.
common_mistakes.fix: Add focused normal and negative tests and record exact expected status/body.

common_mistakes.why: Even short examples may mutate records, reveal data or affect availability.
common_mistakes.fix: Use synthetic inputs and a disposable environment; review security, cleanup and rollback before promotion.
